summary: Announces that the Stanford Electronics Research Lab host SU-DSL, a Very Distant Host, changes from IMP 2 Host 2 to IMP 2 Host 3, moving its address from 130 to 194.

plainLanguage.summary: A computer got a new address on the network, and this note announces it.

subtitle: SU-DSL's network address moves from 130 to 194

tldr.problem: The Stanford Electronics Research Lab very distant host needs to be reassigned from host 2 to host 3 on the same IMP, requiring an address update.
tldr.mechanism: The host location on IMP 2 changes from position 2 to position 3. The network address recalculation reflects this: from 130 to 194.
tldr.outcome: The address change is effective immediately and users and routing systems must be notified of the new network address.

today: RFC 637 is a historical infrastructure notice from the early ARPANET. The address reassignment it announces has no modern relevance beyond its documentation of early network management practices.

sections.title: Address Reassignment
sections.content:
RFC 637 announces an immediate change to the network address of the Stanford Electronics Research Lab (SU-DSL) very distant host. The host was at IMP 2, Host 2, with network address 130. It is now at IMP 2, Host 3, with network address 194. Unlike RFC 634, which announced a move to a different IMP location, this change is within the same IMP facility at Stanford Research Institute (SRI).

The previous host position 2 on IMP 2 will be assigned to a PDP-11 operated by the SRI Artificial Intelligence Center, so the reassignment makes room for that new system.
sections.plainLanguage: A computer's address changed because it switched positions on the same network box, making room for a new computer to use the old spot.

sections.title: Within-IMP Reassignment
sections.content: This address change differs from typical host migrations in that the IMP location remains the same. The SU-DSL host stays on IMP 2 (the SRI connection point) but moves from host slot 2 to host slot 3. The network address reflects this shift: 130 to 194 encodes the new position. Such within-IMP reassignments are common in network management when hosts need to be repositioned or when different organizations at the same site need to connect to different host positions.
sections.plainLanguage: Instead of moving to a different network box, this computer just switched slots on the same box, and a new computer takes its old slot.

sections.title: Immediate Effect
sections.content: The RFC emphasizes that the change is effective immediately—not pending or scheduled for a future date. This immediate effect suggests either that the SU-DSL host had not been connected before or that the change had already occurred physically and the RFC serves to officially announce it to the network community. The notice ensures that all network routing tables and host directories are updated without delay to reflect the new address.
sections.plainLanguage: The address changes right away, not later. All the network computers need to know the new address immediately.
